name: Omni Interactions
desc:
Remote Customer Service Rep (Contractor Role) | $14-$20/hr | Inbound, No Sales Expectations
Company: Omni Interactions
Industry: Business Process Outsourcing / Multi-Client Contract Customer Service
What Your Day Will Look Like:
 Picture yourself as a contractor who answers inbound calls (and sometimes chats or emails) for a rotating mix of well-known companies, since Omni contracts you out to different clients rather than having you work for just one. You build your own schedule within whatever hours each client needs covered, mostly weekdays and daytime. Here's the part that's different from most jobs in this database: you're only paid while you're actively helping a customer (your "phone status"), not for downtime between calls, so your actual earnings depend on how busy your assigned client is and how efficiently you work.
assessment: expect assessments but not clients will have one.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: Not stated in posting.
Required Experience: Not stated by years. Proven customer service track record is called out as a must-have.
Preferred Experience: Not separately broken out.
Required Skills:
Exceptional written and verbal communication
Strong attention to detail and problem solving
Friendly, empathetic, professional tone
Self-motivated and proactive, since there's no direct supervisor watching a shift
Comfortable navigating multiple computer applications and toggling between screens
Minimum typing speed of 25 WPM
Best Fit
 This role is ideal for:
Someone who wants genuine schedule flexibility within daytime and weekday hours
Someone self-disciplined enough to stay productive and hit adherence targets without a manager checking in
Someone comfortable with 1099 contractor pay structure, where earnings depend on active phone time
Someone who already has a laptop or desktop meeting the tech specs, since a device isn't provided
Not a Good Fit for:
Anyone who needs guaranteed hourly pay regardless of call volume
Anyone without a laptop or desktop computer (tablets, Chromebooks, and iPads are explicitly not allowed)
Anyone who can't commit to hardwired internet, since WiFi, satellite, and mobile hotspot connections are not accepted
Anyone who needs W2 benefits like health insurance, PTO, or unemployment coverage
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
Independent contractor customer service
Inbound phone support
Multi-client contract work
Remote customer care
Self-scheduling
Commitment adherence
Technical troubleshooting
Written and verbal communication
Home office setup
Contract-based call handling
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
 This one doesn't follow the standard 4 step process. There's no traditional interview described in the posting. Instead, once selected, you move through a paperwork and verification stage: signing a Master Services Agreement and Statement of Work, submitting a W-9, verifying your identity with a valid government photo ID, and completing a background check (select clients also require a drug test). Total time to hire is not stated.
4-5 things to be ready to speak to during the application and verification process:
Tell us about your customer service background and what "outstanding customer care" looks like to you.
How do you stay productive and self-motivated when no one is directly supervising your shift?
Walk us through your home office setup, computer specs, and internet connection type.
How do you feel about your pay being tied to active phone time rather than a flat hourly rate?
Are you comfortable committing to a set schedule two weeks in advance and maintaining consistent attendance to it
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
Pay: $14 to $20/hr depending on the client you're assigned to. Pay is based on active phone status, not scheduled time, so actual earnings vary with call volume. Additional incentives may be available based on performance targets.
Shift: Mostly weekday and daytime hours, self-scheduled within each client's operating hours. Schedules must be submitted two weeks in advance. Omni's stated business expectation is 18 hours per week scheduled and worked, with 95% schedule adherence expected (meaning you're expected to actually work close to what you scheduled, not just show up loosely close to it).
Benefits: None. This is a 1099 independent contractor role. The posting is explicit that there is no vacation pay, sick leave, retirement benefits, Social Security contribution, workers compensation, health or disability benefits, overtime, or unemployment insurance.
Equipment Provided: Not provided. Participant needs their own computer (Windows 11, 8GB RAM minimum, no tablets or Chromebooks), a wired USB headset, and hardwired high-speed internet (10 Mbps down, 5 Mbps up minimum). A smartphone is also required for daily authentication.
Felony Friendly?: Not stated. A background check is required for everyone, and select clients require a drug test.
Drug Test: Required for select clients only, not universal across all Omni assignments.
Notes: Worth flagging clearly to a participant before they apply: there's a real, out of pocket $40 background check fee they're responsible for (Omni covers the rest of the cost), and pay is tied to active phone time, not just scheduled hours, so this isn't a flat guaranteed hourly rate like most other entries in the database. The commitment adherence tracking (95% target) is also stricter and more formally measured than most contractor roles here, so a participant who struggles with self-managed scheduling may find this one harder to sustain than it first appears. On the positive side, the flexibility to build your own schedule within client hours and work across a variety of well known clients is a genuine plus for someone who wants true contractor independence.
Career Pathway: Not stated directly in the posting. Industry pattern for platforms like this typically means access to more clients and potentially higher paying assignments as tenure and performance build, but that's inferred, not confirmed by Omni directly, so confirm with a participant during onboarding rather than promising it upfront.
training: depends on the client you are assigned to
